stories.title: Explosions on Iran's Qeshm Island as US reportedly strikes in Hormuz
stories.body: Explosions were heard on Iran's Qeshm Island and near Bandar Lengeh late on 2 November. US media, citing officials, reported limited "defensive strikes" on Iranian missile sites after Revolutionary Guards fired at a US aircraft; neither government had confirmed them. At the same time, President Trump said a deal with Iran could happen soon, and Iran said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US lifts its naval blockade. Brent crude rose to about $106.
stories.why: Diplomacy and limited strikes are running side by side, so oil prices, and Nigeria's fuel import bill, remain volatile.

cards.front: What did Iran say it needs before reopening Hormuz within two days (November 2026)?
cards.back: The US must lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports and end hostilities.

stories.title: Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine set for 10–11 November
stories.body: US envoy Steve Witkoff announced US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November. The Kremlin said Russia's delegation will be led by Vladimir Medinsky. President Zelenskyy said he hopes the talks open the way to a meeting with President Putin. European governments will not be at the table, but US envoys are meeting Germany, France, the UK, NATO and the EU in Brussels.
stories.why: A deal would ease pressure on world food and fuel prices that affect Nigeria.

cards.front: Who leads Russia's delegation at the November 2026 Abu Dhabi talks?
cards.back: Vladimir Medinsky, a former culture minister.

stories.title: Bandits abduct 14 Islamic school pupils in Niger State
stories.body: Police confirmed that suspected bandits abducted 14 pupils of an Islamic school and their teacher at Tungan-Bako village, Pandogari district, Rafi LGA, Niger State, on 31 October. The pupils were returning from helping their teacher harvest maize. Police said joint security teams have begun a rescue operation. It follows the abduction of 47 farmers in Mariga LGA in September.
stories.why: School and farm kidnappings in the North-central are a recurring threat and a likely interview topic.

stories.title: Israel heads for coalition talks after hung result
stories.body: With about 90 percent of votes counted, Prime Minister Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was on course for 53 seats and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot for 48, well short of the 61 needed. Arab parties could win a record 19 seats. Eisenkot and Netanyahu have both ruled out a minority government backed by Arab parties. President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders after official results, and Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister.
stories.why: A weaker Netanyahu government could change Israel's approach to Gaza and Iran.

stories.title: Nigeria starts writing a new National Security Strategy
stories.body: National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu inaugurated a 33-member committee to review the 2019 National Security Strategy and draft a new one, NSS 2026. It is chaired by retired Major General Sarkin Bello and must submit a final draft by 27 November. The new strategy is meant to address terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, cybercrime and misinformation.
stories.why: The National Security Strategy is the framework the NIA and other agencies work within, so it is a likely interview question.

cards.front: Which National Security Strategy is Nigeria replacing, and with what?
cards.back: The 2019 NSS, with a new NSS 2026 (committee inaugurated by NSA Ribadu in October 2026).
